title: Option premium is not income
summary: Calling covered call or cash-secured put premium income is misleading. You are not a landlord renting out shares. The premium is closer to a distribution from your own future returns: you take cash now and give up upside later. The word income gives a false sense of security, so understand the risks.

steps.caption: The stock trades at $100. Compare owning shares with selling a $105 call against them.
Shares alone: the full gain or loss of the stock.
The covered call: a small premium now, no gain above $105, and almost the full loss below.
The premium is paid out of your own future upside. That is a trade-off, not rent.
The premium lowers the breakeven only by its own size. The share risk stays.

takeaways: Selling covered calls or cash-secured puts does not create income like rent.
The premium is closer to a distribution from your own future returns.
Calling it income gives a false sense of security about the risk.
caveats: This is the speaker's framing. Prices and strikes in the chart are example values.
